stem:
The diagram shows Hitesh's coil of insulated copper wire wound on an iron nail and joined to a cell. Steel paper clips cling to the nail tip.

Which claim about this arrangement is correct?

options.text: The nail stays strongly magnetic and keeps holding the clips after the current is switched off.
The iron nail core makes the electromagnet weaker than the coil alone.
The current-carrying coil acts as a temporary magnet, and the iron nail core makes it stronger.
Without any current, the coil alone still acts as a strong permanent magnet.

teacher.key_rationale: A current-carrying coil acts as a temporary magnet. An iron core makes that electromagnet stronger; magnetism fades when the current stops.
teacher.figure_note: Coil on iron nail joined to a cell; clips at the tip.
